questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: One construct measured two ways
questions.learningObjective: Avoid assuming measure equivalence
questions.stem: A construct is measured two ways. What should the analyst avoid?

options.text: Assuming the two measures are equivalent without checking

questions.explanation: The analyst should not assume equivalence without checking. Tempting wrong ideas mislabel good practices as errors.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Comparing a finding with a differently sampled rate
questions.learningObjective: Standardise sampling frames
questions.stem: Why is standardising sampling frames important when comparing a finding with a rate?

answer.exemplar: Without standardisation, differences in sampling frames can be mistaken for differences in the underlying phenomenon.

questions.explanation: Unstandardised frames can masquerade as phenomenon differences. The tempting shortcut is to compare raw figures.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: A case set against a rate
questions.learningObjective: Avoid overreading a single case

stimulus.body: A single historical case is set against a population rate. The analyst wants to draw a conclusion.

questions.stem: What should be avoided?

options.text: Treating the case as decisive for the rate

questions.explanation: The case should not be treated as decisive for the rate. Tempting wrong ideas mislabel good practices as errors.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Naming the two fields a question joins
questions.learningObjective: Name fields precisely
questions.stem: A historical question names two fields imprecisely. What is the consequence?

options.text: The analysis may address the wrong question

questions.explanation: Imprecise field names can misdirect the analysis. Tempting wrong ideas judge by length, aesthetics, or popularity.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: A shared artefact used for different purposes
questions.learningObjective: Document an artefact's purposes
questions.stem: An artefact is used for different purposes across arguments. How should this be documented?

options.text: List each purpose with the claim it supports

questions.explanation: Listing each purpose with its claim preserves multiplicity. Tempting wrong ideas ignore, conflate, or delete.
